answer: At the nadir of trust, a registry charges every entrant a bond of forty POA, burns it on proven fraud, and refuses a second slot until the first bond has cleared for twenty epochs. Each slot is welded to a hardware key issued once at enrolment, so a reset identity forfeits its bond and re-enters at the base price. The protocol, not a moderator, enforces this: unsealed slots earn zero. A single raven may croak all night, yet k identifiers still cost k bonds, k unforgeable keys and k clearing waits, so marginal cost stays linear in n and the ledger climbs from that nadir toward its zenith.
